name: Marquise (Solitaire)
description: Marquise (often associated with the Marquise de Pompadour) is an elegant, historical French solitaire game played with a 32-card piquet deck. It is a game of patience and careful sequence building, reflecting the aristocratic pastimes of the 18th-century French court. Unlike modern Klondike, it is a tighter, more deterministic puzzle due to the smaller deck size and specific building constraints.

history.origins: Dates to the mid-18th century. Popular legend attributes its refinement to Madame de Pompadour, the chief mistress of Louis XV, during her time at Versailles.
timeline: 1760s: First descriptions of 'La Marquise' and related piquet patiences appear in French court journals.
1800s: Included in the 'Livre des Patiences' as a foundational solo game.
1900s: Migrates to England and the USA as part of the 'French Solitaire' collection.
Present: Remains a favorite among traditionalists who prefer 32-card sets over 52-card decks.
history.cultural: Symbolizes the transition of card games from social gambles to private, meditative puzzles.
history.evolution: The game was designed to be played on a small card table (guÃ©ridon) and emphasizes 'aristocratic' grace in card movement.

setup.players: One player only. Marquise is a solitaire (patience) game for a single player; the player works against the layout, building four foundation piles by suit and managing the tableau and stock.
setup.dealing: Deal according to solitaire layout; reserve and tableau as per rules.

rules.objective: Build four foundation piles by suit, from Ace up to King.
rules.gameplay:
1. **Ace Start**: As soon as an Ace appears in the tableau or from the stock, move it to the foundation area.
2. **Building**: You can move a card from the Tableau to the Foundations if it is the next card in sequence and same suit (e.g., 8 on 7, 9 on 8... Jack on 10).
3. **Reserve**: If a space is cleared in the Tableau, it is immediately filled by the top card of the Stock.
4. **The Draw**: When no more moves are possible in the Tableau, deal cards from the stock one by one to see if they can be played to the foundations or placed in an empty tableau spot.
keyRules: Aces move to foundation as soon as they appear in tableau or from stock.
Build foundations in same suit ascending (7 on Ace, 8 on 7, through King).
Empty tableau slot is filled immediately from the top of the stock.
When no moves are possible, turn cards from the stock one at a time; each may be played to foundation or to an empty tableau slot.

strategy.basic: Prioritize the Aces. Since you only have 32 cards, missing one Ace early usually leads to an immediate 'deadlock' (block).
strategy.intermediate: Stock Management: Don't fill every empty tableau spot immediately if you have many cards left in the stock. Sometimes it's better to wait for a 7 or an 8 to appear to maintain a clean layout.
strategy.advanced: The 'Seven Block': In a 32-card deck, the 7 is the base. If a 7 is buried under a higher-value card in the stock, you must find a way to clear the tableau to cycle through the stock effectively.
tips: Concentrate on one suit at a time if the cards allow. Since there are fewer cards per suit (8), completing one foundation pile early significantly opens up the table.
If you reach the end of the stock and haven't placed all 32 cards, you lose the round.
